name: Polarization in Conductors
text: When a charged object is brought near a conductor, the free electrons in the conductor shift toward or away from the charged object. This creates regions of positive and negative charge within the conductor, even though the overall object remains neutral.This separation of charge means that one side of the conductor is attracted to the charged object, leading to a noticeable force. The effect disappears once the charged object is removed, as the electrons return to their original positions.

images.alt: Polarization in Conductors. Mobile electrons redistribute within a neutral conductor.

name: Polarization in Insulators
text: In insulators, electrons are not free to move across the material, but the atoms or molecules can reorient slightly. This means that the negative and positive charges within each molecule shift just a bit, creating tiny dipoles throughout the material.Although the charges don't move far, the overall effect is enough to cause the insulator to be attracted to a charged object. This is why a charged balloon can stick to a wall, even though the wall is neutral.

images.alt: Polarization in Insulators. Bound charges shift within molecules; electrons do not flow freely across the insulator.

name: Attraction of Neutral Objects
text: Polarization explains why neutral objects, like bits of paper, are attracted to a charged comb or rod. The charges in the paper rearrange, making one side slightly more positive or negative, which is then pulled toward the charged object.This attraction happens even though no electrons are transferred between the objects. It's a temporary effect that lasts only while the charged object is nearby.

images.alt: Attraction of Neutral Objects. Opposite charge is nearer the rod, so attraction can exceed the more distant repulsion.

name: No Net Charge Transfer
text: During polarization, there is no actual movement of electrons from one object to another. Instead, charges shift positions within the object, creating regions of slight positive and negative charge.Once the external charged object is removed, the charges in the neutral object return to their original arrangement, and the attraction disappears.

images.alt: No Net Charge Transfer. Polarization redistributes charge inside an object without transferring net charge across the gap.
